arithmetic-basics.must: Multiplication and division are done before addition and subtraction, unless brackets say otherwise.
arithmetic-basics.fix: Brackets first, then times and divide, then plus and minus.

arithmetic-basics.must: Subtraction and division depend on order: 8 - 3 is not 3 - 8.
arithmetic-basics.fix: Swapping the numbers changes the answer for minus and divide, not for plus and times.

arithmetic-basics.must: Multiplying is repeated adding: 4 × 3 means four threes.

fractions-decimals.must: A fraction is equal parts: the bottom is how many parts, the top is how many you have.
fractions-decimals.fix: The bottom number splits the whole into equal parts; the top counts them.

fractions-decimals.must: To add fractions, the bottoms must match first.
fractions-decimals.fix: Make the bottoms the same, then add only the tops.

fractions-decimals.must: A decimal is a fraction with a bottom of 10, 100, 1000 and so on.
fractions-decimals.fix: 0.25 means 25 hundredths, which is one quarter.

powers-roots.must: A power means repeated multiplying: 2 to the 3 is 2 × 2 × 2.
powers-roots.fix: 2 cubed is 2 times 2 times 2, which is 8, not 6.

powers-roots.must: A square root undoes squaring: the root of 9 is 3 because 3 × 3 is 9.
powers-roots.fix: The root asks: which number times itself gives this?
Any non-zero number to the power zero is 1.

ratios-percentages.must: A ratio compares amounts: 2:3 means 2 parts for every 3 parts.
ratios-percentages.fix: 2 to 3 means for every 2 of one, there are 3 of the other.
Percent means per hundred: 40% is 40 out of 100.

ratios-percentages.must: A percentage of something is a fraction of it: 25% of 80 is a quarter of 80.
ratios-percentages.fix: Turn the percent into a fraction or decimal, then multiply.

coordinates.must: A point is written (x, y): x is across, y is up.
The origin (0, 0) is where the axes cross.
coordinates.fix: Every point is measured from the origin, where both axes are zero.

coordinates.must: Negative x is left of the origin, negative y is below it.
coordinates.fix: Minus x goes left, minus y goes down.

scientific-notation.must: A number is written as a number between 1 and 10 times a power of ten.
scientific-notation.fix: Write it as one digit before the point, times ten to some power.

scientific-notation.must: A positive power makes the number big, a negative power makes it small.
scientific-notation.fix: Ten to the minus 3 means divide by a thousand.

scientific-notation.must: The power counts how many places the decimal point moves.
scientific-notation.fix: Each step in the power moves the decimal point one place.

particles-matter.must: All matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving.
particles-matter.fix: Even in a solid, the particles never stop jiggling.

particles-matter.must: In solids particles are packed and vibrate; in liquids they slide past each other; in gases they spread out fast.
particles-matter.fix: Solid: packed and shaking. Liquid: close but sliding. Gas: far apart and fast.

particles-matter.common_wrong: particles themselves get bigger when hot
particles-matter.fix: Heat makes particles move faster and spread out; the particles don't grow.

units-si.must: SI base units include metre, kilogram, second, ampere and kelvin.
units-si.fix: Length in metres, mass in kilograms, time in seconds.

units-si.must: Prefixes scale units: kilo is a thousand, milli is a thousandth.
units-si.fix: Kilo means times a thousand; milli means divided by a thousand.

units-si.must: Always convert to the same units before calculating.
units-si.fix: Change everything to base units first, then put numbers in the formula.

geometry-basics.must: Angles on a straight line add to 180 degrees.
geometry-basics.fix: A straight line is a half turn: 180 degrees.

geometry-basics.must: Angles in a triangle add to 180 degrees.
geometry-basics.fix: The three angles of any triangle always add to 180.
All the way round is 360 degrees.

pythagoras.must: It only works in right-angled triangles.
The square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two.
pythagoras.fix: Longest side squared equals the other two sides squared, added.

pythagoras.must: The longest side, the hypotenuse, is opposite the right angle.
pythagoras.fix: The hypotenuse faces the right angle and is always the longest.

trig-ratios.must: Sine is opposite over hypotenuse, cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse, tangent is opposite over adjacent.
trig-ratios.fix: SOH CAH TOA: sine opposite-hypotenuse, cosine adjacent-hypotenuse, tangent opposite-adjacent.

trig-ratios.must: Opposite and adjacent depend on which angle you're looking at.
trig-ratios.fix: Opposite is across from your angle; adjacent touches it.

trig-ratios.must: The ratios work for right-angled triangles.
trig-ratios.fix: These ratios come from a right-angled triangle.

algebra-basics.must: A letter stands for an unknown number.
algebra-basics.fix: x is just a number we don't know yet.

algebra-basics.must: Only like terms can be added: 3x + 2x is 5x, but 3x + 2 stays as it is.
algebra-basics.fix: You can only combine terms with the same letter part.
A number next to a letter means multiply.

forces-basics.must: A force is a push or a pull.
forces-basics.fix: Every force is a push or a pull on something.
A force has a size in newtons and a direction.

forces-basics.must: Balanced forces cause no change in motion.
forces-basics.common_wrong: if forces are balanced the object must be still
forces-basics.fix: Balanced forces mean no change: still stays still, moving keeps moving steadily.

vectors-basics.must: A vector has both size and direction.
vectors-basics.fix: A vector tells you how much and which way.
Put the second arrow at the tip of the first; the result goes start to finish.

vectors-basics.must: A vector can be split into horizontal and vertical parts.
vectors-basics.fix: Any arrow is an across part plus an up part.

scalars-vectors.must: A scalar has only size; a vector has size and direction.
scalars-vectors.fix: Scalar: just how much. Vector: how much and which way.

scalars-vectors.must: Speed and distance are scalars; velocity and displacement are vectors.
scalars-vectors.common_wrong: speed and velocity are the same
scalars-vectors.fix: Velocity is speed with a direction.

scalars-vectors.must: Mass is a scalar but weight is a vector.
scalars-vectors.fix: Weight is a force, so it has a direction: down.

functions.must: A function gives exactly one output for each input.
functions.fix: Each input goes in and exactly one output comes out.

functions.must: f(x) means the output when the input is x.
functions.fix: f of x is the output for input x, not f times x.

functions.must: The domain is the allowed inputs; the range is the possible outputs.
functions.fix: Domain: what can go in. Range: what can come out.

graphs-and-slope.must: Slope is rise over run: how much y changes for each step in x.
graphs-and-slope.fix: Slope is up divided by across.

graphs-and-slope.must: A positive slope goes up to the right; a negative slope goes down.
graphs-and-slope.fix: Uphill to the right is positive, downhill is negative.

graphs-and-slope.must: A steeper line has a bigger slope.
graphs-and-slope.fix: The steeper the line, the bigger the number.

area-volume.must: Area measures flat space in square units; volume measures space in cubic units.
area-volume.fix: Area is in squares, like square metres; volume in cubes.

area-volume.must: Rectangle area is length times width.
area-volume.fix: Multiply the two sides for a rectangle's area.

area-volume.must: A prism's volume is its cross-section area times its length.
area-volume.fix: Find the end face area, then multiply by how long it is.

energy-basics.must: Energy can't be created or destroyed, only moved or changed into another form.
energy-basics.fix: Energy is never used up; it moves to another store, often heat.
The unit of energy is the joule.

energy-basics.must: Moving things have kinetic energy; raised things have gravitational potential energy.
energy-basics.fix: Motion means kinetic energy; height means potential energy.

speed-basics.must: Speed is distance divided by time.
Average speed uses the total distance and the total time.
speed-basics.fix: Use total distance over total time, not the average of the speeds.

speed-basics.must: Speed is measured in metres per second (or km per hour).
speed-basics.fix: In physics, speed is usually in metres per second.

displacement-velocity.must: Displacement is how far from the start in a straight line, with direction.
displacement-velocity.common_wrong: displacement is the same as distance
displacement-velocity.fix: Walk round a track and back: big distance, zero displacement.

displacement-velocity.must: Velocity is displacement divided by time.
displacement-velocity.fix: Velocity is how fast and which way.

displacement-velocity.must: Velocity can be negative when moving the other way.
displacement-velocity.fix: A minus sign on velocity just means the opposite direction.

linear-equations.must: Do the same thing to both sides to keep the equation balanced.
linear-equations.fix: Whatever you do to one side, do to the other.

linear-equations.must: Undo operations in reverse order to get x alone.
linear-equations.fix: Undo the adding first, then the multiplying.

linear-equations.must: Check by putting the answer back into the equation.
linear-equations.fix: Put your x back in; both sides should match.

acceleration.must: Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes: change in velocity divided by time.
acceleration.fix: Acceleration is change in velocity per second.

acceleration.must: It's measured in metres per second squared.
acceleration.fix: The unit is metres per second, per second.

acceleration.must: Slowing down or changing direction is also acceleration.
acceleration.fix: Braking and turning are accelerations too.

radians.must: A radian is the angle where the arc length equals the radius.
radians.fix: One radian: the arc is as long as the radius.

radians.must: A full turn is 2π radians, so 180 degrees is π radians.
radians.fix: Half a turn is pi radians, a full turn 2 pi.

radians.must: Arc length is radius times angle in radians.
radians.fix: Arc length equals r times the angle, in radians.

newtons-first-law.must: An object keeps its velocity (still or moving steadily) unless a net force acts.
newtons-first-law.common_wrong: moving things need a force to keep moving
newtons-first-law.fix: No net force means no change: moving things keep moving.

newtons-first-law.must: Things slow down in real life because of friction and air resistance.
newtons-first-law.fix: Friction is the force that slows things, not a lack of push.

newtons-first-law.must: Inertia is the tendency to resist changes in motion; more mass means more inertia.
newtons-first-law.fix: Heavier things are harder to start and stop.

free-body-diagrams.must: Draw only the forces acting on the one object.
free-body-diagrams.common_wrong: include forces the object puts on others
free-body-diagrams.fix: Only arrows for forces on this object, not forces it exerts.

free-body-diagrams.must: Each arrow shows the force's direction, and its length shows the size.
free-body-diagrams.fix: Arrow direction is the force's direction; longer means bigger.

free-body-diagrams.must: Label each force, such as weight, normal force, friction, tension.
free-body-diagrams.fix: Name every arrow so you know which force it is.

trig-functions.must: Sine and cosine graphs are waves that repeat every 360 degrees (2π).
trig-functions.fix: Sine and cosine repeat every full turn.

trig-functions.must: Sine and cosine stay between -1 and 1.
trig-functions.fix: They never go above 1 or below minus 1.

trig-functions.must: Cosine is the sine wave shifted by 90 degrees.
trig-functions.fix: Cosine is the same wave as sine, moved over a quarter turn.

coulombs-law.must: The force between two charges is proportional to the product of the charges.
The force gets weaker with the square of the distance.
coulombs-law.common_wrong: double the distance, half the force
coulombs-law.fix: Double the distance and the force drops to a quarter.

coulombs-law.must: Like charges repel, opposite charges attract.
coulombs-law.fix: Same signs push apart; opposite signs pull together.

newtons-second-law.must: Net force equals mass times acceleration.
newtons-second-law.common_wrong: a force is needed to keep moving
newtons-second-law.fix: Force changes motion: F equals m times a.

newtons-second-law.must: More mass needs more force for the same acceleration.
newtons-second-law.fix: A heavier thing needs a bigger push to speed up the same.

newtons-second-law.must: Acceleration is in the direction of the net force.
newtons-second-law.fix: It speeds up in the direction of the total push.
One newton speeds 1 kilogram up by 1 metre per second, every second.

indices-surds.must: When multiplying powers of the same base, add the powers.
indices-surds.fix: x squared times x cubed is x to the five: add the powers.

indices-surds.must: A negative power means one over: x to the minus 1 is 1 over x.
indices-surds.fix: Negative power means divide: flip it to one over.

indices-surds.must: A surd is a root that can't be simplified to a whole number, like root 2.
indices-surds.fix: Root 2 can't be written exactly as a fraction, so we keep it as a root.

work-done.must: Work done is force times distance moved in the direction of the force.
work-done.fix: Work equals force times distance along the force.

work-done.must: Work is energy transferred, measured in joules.
work-done.fix: Doing work moves energy; both are in joules.

work-done.must: No movement in the force's direction means no work is done.
work-done.common_wrong: holding something heavy still does work
work-done.fix: Holding a bag still does no work in physics: nothing moves.

electric-current.must: Current is the rate of flow of charge: charge divided by time.
electric-current.fix: Current is how much charge passes each second.

electric-current.must: Current is not used up in a circuit; it's the same all the way round a single loop.
electric-current.fix: Current is the same before and after a bulb; energy is what's transferred.

elasticity.must: An elastic object returns to its shape when the force is removed.
Hooke's law: extension is proportional to force, up to the limit of proportionality.
elasticity.fix: Double the force, double the stretch, until the limit.

elasticity.must: Past the elastic limit the object is permanently stretched.
elasticity.fix: Stretch too far and it won't go back.

shm.must: In simple harmonic motion the acceleration is proportional to the displacement and points back to the middle.
shm.fix: The further from the middle, the stronger the pull back.

shm.must: The period doesn't depend on the amplitude.
shm.fix: Small or big swings take the same time for true simple harmonic motion.

shm.must: Speed is greatest at the middle and zero at the ends.
shm.fix: Fastest through the centre, momentarily still at each end.

electric-field.must: An electric field is the region where a charge feels a force.
electric-field.fix: A field is where a charge would get pushed or pulled.

electric-field.must: Field strength is force per unit charge.
electric-field.fix: Field strength equals force divided by charge.

electric-field.must: Field lines point the way a positive charge would move.
electric-field.fix: Arrows go away from positive and towards negative.

straight-lines.must: A straight line can be written y = mx + c.
straight-lines.fix: Every straight line fits y equals m x plus c.

straight-lines.must: m is the gradient and c is where the line crosses the y-axis.
straight-lines.fix: m is the slope; c is where it crosses the y-axis.

straight-lines.must: Parallel lines have the same gradient.
straight-lines.fix: Same slope means the lines never meet.

waves-basics.must: Waves transfer energy without transferring matter.
waves-basics.common_wrong: the water moves along with the wave
waves-basics.fix: The wave moves on; the water mostly bobs up and down.

waves-basics.must: Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength.
Transverse waves vibrate across the direction of travel; longitudinal waves vibrate along it.
waves-basics.fix: Transverse shakes sideways; longitudinal squashes and stretches along.

limits.must: A limit is the value a function gets closer and closer to as x approaches a number.
limits.fix: A limit is where the function is heading.

limits.must: The function doesn't have to actually reach that value, or even be defined there.
limits.common_wrong: the limit is just the value at that point
limits.fix: The limit can exist even where the function has a hole.

limits.must: Limits are the basis for derivatives.
limits.fix: Derivatives are built from limits of tiny changes.

derivatives-basics.must: A derivative is the rate of change: the slope of the curve at one point.
derivatives-basics.fix: The derivative is the slope of the tangent at that point.

derivatives-basics.must: It comes from the limit of change in y over change in x as the change gets tiny.
derivatives-basics.fix: Shrink the gap between two points until it's almost zero.

derivatives-basics.must: A derivative of zero means a flat point, like a peak or a dip.
derivatives-basics.fix: Zero slope means flat: a top, a bottom, or a pause.

differentiation-rules.must: Power rule: the derivative of x to the n is n times x to the n minus 1.
differentiation-rules.fix: Bring the power down in front, then lower the power by one.

differentiation-rules.must: The derivative of a constant is zero.
differentiation-rules.fix: A constant doesn't change, so its derivative is zero.

differentiation-rules.must: You differentiate a sum term by term.
differentiation-rules.fix: Differentiate each piece separately, then add them.

what-is-a-program.must: A program is a list of exact steps the computer follows.
what-is-a-program.fix: A program is exact steps; the computer follows them literally.

what-is-a-program.must: Steps run in order, top to bottom, unless the code jumps.
what-is-a-program.fix: Lines run top to bottom, one at a time.

what-is-a-program.must: The computer does what you wrote, not what you meant.
what-is-a-program.common_wrong: the computer understands what you meant
what-is-a-program.fix: It never guesses: it does exactly what the code says.

variables-values.must: A variable is a name that refers to a value.
variables-values.fix: A variable is a name tag on a value.

variables-values.must: Assigning again replaces the old value.
variables-values.common_wrong: a variable keeps all its old values
variables-values.fix: After x = 5 then x = 7, x is only 7.

variables-values.must: The right side of = is worked out first.
variables-values.fix: The right side is calculated first, then named.

data-types.must: Values have types such as int, float, string and boolean.
data-types.fix: Every value has a kind: number, text, or true/false.

data-types.must: Text and numbers are different even if they look alike.
Mixing types can cause errors unless you convert.
data-types.fix: Convert first, like int("7"), before adding to a number.

operators-expressions.must: Operators combine values into an expression that gives one value.
operators-expressions.fix: An expression works out to a single value.

operators-expressions.must: Multiply and divide come before add and subtract.

booleans-comparisons.fix: A comparison answers yes or no: True or False.
Use == to compare and = to give a value.

booleans-comparisons.must: and needs both true; or needs at least one.
booleans-comparisons.fix: and: both must be true. or: one is enough.

strings-text.must: A string is text in quotes, a row of characters.
strings-text.fix: A string is text: characters in a row, in quotes.

strings-text.common_wrong: the first character is at position 1
strings-text.fix: The first character is at position 0.

input-output.must: Input is data going into a program; output is what comes out.
input-output.fix: Input goes in, output comes out.

input-output.must: input() gives text, so numbers need converting.
input-output.fix: Wrap input() in int() to get a number.

input-output.must: print() shows output on the screen.
input-output.fix: print() displays text; it doesn't return it.

conditionals.must: An if runs its code only when the condition is True.
conditionals.fix: The if block runs only when its condition is True.

conditionals.must: else runs when the condition is False.
conditionals.fix: else is the other path, for when the condition fails.

conditionals.must: Only one branch of an if-elif-else chain runs.
conditionals.fix: The first true branch runs, then the rest are skipped.

loops.must: A loop repeats a block of code.
loops.fix: A loop runs the same code again and again.

loops.must: for repeats a set number of times or once per item.
loops.fix: for goes through a range or each item in a list.

loops.must: while repeats until its condition becomes False.
loops.common_wrong: a while loop stops by itself
loops.fix: while keeps going until its condition turns False; it must be able to change.

lists-arrays.must: A list stores many values in order.
lists-arrays.fix: A list keeps values in order in one place.

lists-arrays.must: Items are found by index, starting at 0.
lists-arrays.common_wrong: the first item is at index 1

lists-arrays.must: len() gives the number of items.
lists-arrays.fix: len(xs) tells you how many items there are.

functions-programming.must: A function is a named, reusable set of steps.
functions-programming.fix: Write the steps once, then call them by name.

functions-programming.must: Parameters are inputs; return sends a result back.
functions-programming.fix: Inputs go in as parameters; return gives the answer back.

functions-programming.must: Defining a function doesn't run it; calling it does.
functions-programming.fix: def only defines it; call it to run it.

scope.must: Variables made inside a function are local to it.
scope.fix: Names made inside a function stay inside it.

scope.must: Code outside a function can't see its local variables.
scope.common_wrong: you can use a function's variables anywhere
scope.fix: Outside the function, its local names don't exist.

scope.must: Functions share results by returning them.
scope.fix: Return the value to use it outside.

dictionaries.must: A dictionary stores values under unique keys.
dictionaries.fix: Each value sits under its own key, like a labelled drawer.

dictionaries.must: You look values up by key, not position.
dictionaries.common_wrong: dictionaries are looked up by position
dictionaries.fix: Use d[key], not a number position.

dictionaries.must: Setting an existing key replaces its value.
dictionaries.fix: Assigning to a key that exists overwrites it.

debugging.must: Read the error message first: it names the problem and line.
debugging.fix: Start with the error message and its line number.

debugging.must: Test one guess at a time.
debugging.fix: Change one thing, re-run, and see what changed.

debugging.must: Print values to check what the program really holds.
debugging.common_wrong: you can tell what a value is by reading the code
debugging.fix: Print the value instead of assuming it.

algorithms-basics.must: An algorithm is clear steps that always finish and solve the problem.
algorithms-basics.fix: Clear steps, always ending with an answer.
First make it right, then make it fast.

algorithms-basics.must: Test edge cases like an empty list.
algorithms-basics.fix: Try the unusual inputs too, like empty or one item.

recursion.must: Recursion is a function calling itself on a smaller problem.
recursion.fix: It solves a big problem by solving a smaller copy.

recursion.must: It needs a base case that stops the calls.
recursion.fix: The base case answers directly and stops it.

recursion.must: Each step must move closer to the base case.
recursion.fix: Each call must make the problem smaller.

searching-sorting.fix: Sorting arranges items from smallest to largest, or by another rule.

searching-sorting.must: Binary search halves a sorted list each step.
searching-sorting.fix: Check the middle and throw away half, again and again.

searching-sorting.must: Binary search only works on sorted data.
searching-sorting.common_wrong: binary search works on any list
searching-sorting.fix: Sort first, or binary search gives wrong answers.

big-o.must: Big O describes how work grows as input grows.
big-o.common_wrong: Big O is the exact running time
big-o.fix: Big O is about growth, not exact seconds.

big-o.must: A loop inside a loop over n is O(n squared).
big-o.fix: Nested loops over n items do about n times n steps.

big-o.must: O(log n) grows much slower than O(n).
big-o.fix: Halving each step grows very slowly: log n.

objects-classes.must: A class is a template; objects are made from it.
objects-classes.fix: The class is the cutter; objects are the cookies.

objects-classes.must: Each object has its own attribute values.
objects-classes.common_wrong: changing one object changes all of them
objects-classes.fix: Changing one object doesn't change the others.

objects-classes.must: Methods are functions that belong to the class.
objects-classes.fix: Methods are the actions objects can do.

stacks-queues.must: A stack is last in, first out.
stacks-queues.fix: The newest item on a stack leaves first.

stacks-queues.must: A queue is first in, first out.
stacks-queues.common_wrong: a queue takes the newest item first
stacks-queues.fix: The oldest item in a queue leaves first.

stacks-queues.must: Function calls are kept on a stack.
stacks-queues.fix: Each call waits on the stack until the one above it finishes.

trees-graphs.must: A graph is nodes joined by edges.
trees-graphs.fix: Dots are nodes, lines are edges.

trees-graphs.must: A tree has one root and no loops.
trees-graphs.fix: A tree has a single root and never loops back.

trees-graphs.must: Leaves are tree nodes with no children.
trees-graphs.fix: Leaves are at the ends: they have no children.

files-databases.must: Files keep data after the program ends.
files-databases.fix: Save to a file so the data survives a restart.

files-databases.must: A database stores records you can search and update.
files-databases.fix: A database is organised records with the same fields.

files-databases.must: Opening a file for writing replaces its contents.
files-databases.common_wrong: writing to a file always adds to it
files-databases.fix: Mode "w" wipes the file; use "a" to add.

internet-web.must: The browser sends a request; the server sends a response.
DNS turns a website name into an address.
internet-web.fix: DNS works like phone contacts: name to number.

internet-web.common_wrong: a page is sent in one piece
internet-web.fix: Pages arrive in many small packets, put back together.

version-control-git.must: A commit is a saved snapshot with a message.
version-control-git.fix: Each commit saves the project's state, with a note.

version-control-git.must: Branches let you work separately; merging combines them.
version-control-git.fix: Try ideas on a branch, then merge them back.

version-control-git.must: A merge conflict means two changes touched the same lines.
version-control-git.common_wrong: a merge conflict means the project is broken
version-control-git.fix: Conflicts are normal: choose which change to keep.
